exemplars.title: When Refreshable Tactile Displays Meet Conversational Agents: Investigating Accessible Data Presentation and Analysis with Touch and Speech
exemplars.why: A 40-by-60 actuated pin array turns generated graphics into refreshable physical relief that users explore by touch, making material arrangement—not a rendered screen—the load-bearing output channel.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Generative Muscle Stimulation because its tangible output mechanism is equally explicit but supports a broader range of tasks with fewer safety and calibration constraints.

exemplars.title: Shape n' Swarm: Hands-on, Shape-aware Generative Authoring with Swarm UI and LLMs
exemplars.why: Users issue spatial commands by physically arranging tabletop robots and supplementing that arrangement with speech, after which the same embodied elements perform the authored animation—a complete tangible input-and-output loop.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above Generative Muscle Stimulation because it demonstrates both graspable spatial authoring and physical output while offering a more transferable interaction structure and fewer safety constraints.

exemplars.title: Generative Muscle Stimulation: Providing Users with Physical Assistance by Constraining Multimodal-AI with Embodied Knowledge
exemplars.why: The system delivers an AI-generated instruction through EMS-induced finger, wrist, shoulder, and elbow movements, so bodily actuation itself—not a displayed representation—constitutes the output.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above StoryCube because the evidence specifies the physical output mechanism joint by joint, whereas StoryCube establishes tangible prompt composition but provides less detail about how token arrangements are sensed or interpreted.

notes: The selected set preserves the consensus top three but swaps the two tied 4.60 candidates: Shape n’ Swarm ranks second because it provides the most complete and broadly reusable tangible loop, while Generative Muscle Stimulation ranks third because specialized hardware, calibration, agency, and safety concerns constrain transfer. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust any implication of demonstrated outcome gains: the supplied evidence consists of isolated abstract, figure, or system-description excerpts. It establishes interface structure well, but does not consistently establish evaluation results, implementation robustness, user control, or real-world deployment.
